name: Around A
classification_notes: A geometric sans built from circle-triangle-square logic in the tradition of Kabel and Futura, with Arabic-inspired connective forms in letters such as a, f, g, t, u, r and y, keeping it in the geometric sans-serif category.
summary: A geometric sans that borrows Arabic connective logic and early twentieth-century geometric forms, originally cut for a Cali hotel.
description: Around A began as a custom face for the Mudéjar Hotel in Cali, Colombia, formalising a parallel between Arabic script connectivity and Latin geometric sans letterforms drawn from Kabel, Erbar-Grotesk and Futura. Five weights combine circular bowls with sharp-apex capitals for a warm, nostalgic geometric sans.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe Around as a typeface family based on three parameters: Arabic-influenced connectivity, forms built from circle, triangle and square, and rhythm drawn from West Berlin traffic-sign lettering.

name: Around B
subcategory: bold display companion to a geometric sans
classification_notes: A bolder, more daring display companion to Around A built for logos and magazine titles, placing it in the display category despite sharing Around's geometric sans skeleton.
summary: A bolder, eye-catching bonus cut of Around built for logos and magazine titles.
description: Around B takes the Around system into bolder, more daring territory, with slanted strokes drawn from a 1970 Avant Garde magazine lettering piece and ligatures based on a discarded 1960 Walter Ballmer logo for Olivetti. Five weights make it suited to logos and magazine mastheads.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón call Around B an exciting bonus title offering bolder and more daring design options, with a fun and eye-catching look perfect for logos and magazine titles.

name: Ballmer
classification_notes: A sans-serif stripped of Times New Roman's serifs while keeping its proportions, placing it in the humanist sans category with a vintage-inspired structure.
summary: A sans-serif reimagining of Times New Roman's proportions without the serifs, currently in Regular and Oblique.
description: Ballmer strips the serifs from Times New Roman's classic proportions for a clean, contemporary result that still reads as vintage-inspired. This first release covers Regular and Oblique, with further weights planned as the family expands.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe Ballmer as reimagining the classic elegance of Times New Roman, stripping away serifs for a clean, contemporary feel that balances tradition and refinement.

name: Cepelin
subcategory: display serif with rounded ball terminals
classification_notes: A high-contrast serif with rounded, droplet-like terminals gives Cepelin a display serif classification.
summary: A high-contrast display serif with soft, rounded ball terminals.
description: Cepelin is a display serif built around rounded, droplet-shaped terminals and generous contrast, suited to exhibition titling and editorial headlines. It is currently offered in a single Regular style.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón present Cepelin through a live specimen rather than a written brief, letting the rounded terminals and contrast speak for themselves.

name: Chroma Sans
classification_notes: Organic, accentuated shapes with a handcrafted feel place Chroma Sans in the organic display sans category.
summary: A handcrafted, organic-shaped sans in nine weights, originally commissioned for a brand identity project.
description: Chroma Sans was built around the idea of 'Splendid': magnificent, gorgeous, sumptuous. Its organic, accentuated shapes give each character a distinct personality across nine weights, with stylistic alternates for a, f, g and l. It began as a commissioned identity project for Regio before its retail release.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe Chroma Sans as having a particular personality in the ecosystem of typefaces, where each character draws attention due to its organic shapes.

name: Compilation Grotesk
classification_notes: A grotesque sans inspired by wood-type headliners, built around a variable height axis rather than conventional weights, keeping it in the grotesque display category.
summary: A variable-height grotesque display face inspired by wood-type headliners, expanding glyphs upward without stretching them.
description: Compilation Grotesk is a variable font built mainly around the Matterhorn Headliners 2 wood-type tradition. Its height axis lets glyphs stretch upward from the baseline as values rise from 700 to 1100, adjusting rather than distorting proportions and contrast across nine styles.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe it as a variable font concept that includes 9 sort of adjustable heights, letting the system keep contrast and proportions rather than stretching the glyphs out.

name: Prody
classification_notes: Inspired by Cheltenham, Belwe and Souvenir, its soft endings and rounded terminals place Prody in the serif category with a warm, rounded personality.
summary: A clean, elegant serif with soft rounded terminals, inspired by Cheltenham, Belwe and Souvenir.
description: Prody is a modern serif with strong personality thanks to its soft endings and rounded terminals, built for complex professional typography across four weights. Its references sit firmly in the Cheltenham and Souvenir school of rounded American serifs.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe Prody as a clean, elegant and modern serif with a strong personality thanks to its soft endings and rounded terminals.

name: Reclett
classification_notes: Retains the rhythm and modulation of a text serif translated into a stripped sans-serif form, placing it in the humanist sans category as a companion project to Ballmer.
summary: A contemporary sans with a serif soul, translating classical text-face proportions into a stripped sans-serif form.
description: Reclett grew out of an exploration of MN Latin and the earlier Ballmer project into its own distinct system. It keeps the rhythm, proportions and modulation of traditional text faces while presenting them as a clean, system-driven sans across four weights.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón call Reclett a contemporary sans-serif rooted in the logic of classical typography, a serif soul in a sans body bridging editorial heritage with modern clarity.

name: Sweep Poster
classification_notes: A calligraphic reinterpretation of Caslon using a broad nib pen, mixing geometric and organic shapes, placing it in the experimental serif category.
summary: A calligraphic reinterpretation of Caslon, delicate as an Extra Light and dramatic as a Bold poster face.
description: Sweep Poster reworks Caslon's letterforms through a calligraphic nib-pen exploration, mixing geometric and organic strokes into a harmonic, textured serif. Eight weights run from a delicate Extra Light to an impressive Bold, available as static fonts or a variable font.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe it as a modern, elegant and experimental serif typeface, delicate in its Extra Light version and impressive in the Bolder style.

name: Ocelot
classification_notes: Based on George Nesbitt's Gothic, Ocelot keeps that face's grotesque curves and idiosyncrasies, placing it in the grotesque category.
summary: A grotesque built for bold uppercase settings, updating George Nesbitt's Gothic for modern use.
description: Ocelot is designed mainly for uppercase-bold typesetting, based on GOTHIC as originally drawn by George Nesbitt. It keeps that face's easy-going curves and idiosyncrasies across six weights with italics, updated for contemporary use.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe Ocelot as designed mainly for those who adore uppercase-bold fonts, keeping GOTHIC's easy-going curves while updating it for modern use.

name: Vallejo
classification_notes: A hybrid of Albertus and Friz Quadrata with flared, oversized serifs places Vallejo in the flared serif display category.
summary: A flared-serif display face hybridising Albertus and Friz Quadrata, recommended for headlines.
description: Vallejo hybridises two popular reference faces, Albertus and Friz Quadrata, matching their flared and oversized serifs into a single versatile display family. Two weights, Regular and Black, adapt to a wide range of typographic compositions, best suited to headline use.
foundry_blurb: Estudio Calderón describe Vallejo as a serif display type family inspired by Albertus and Friz Quadrata, versatile enough for many sorts of typographic compositions, recommended for headlines.
